        Liquibase JSON changelogs in src/main/resources/db/changelog/ create and version every
        platform table; Hibernate is reduced to schema validation (DIRIGIBLE_DATABASE_SYSTEM_DDL_AUTO
        defaults to "validate") and no longer issues DDL during application startup.
        Dynamic user entities (TypeScript @Entity via data-store, Java @Entity via
        data-store-java) continue to use Hibernate's hbm2ddl=update because their schema is
        authored by end-user code, not by changelogs.

items.title:
org.eclipse.dirigible:dirigible-components-core-java 14.67.0 发布, Lightweight runtime primitives shared between components/engine/engine-java (the full
        client-Java engine — synchronizer, compiler, ClassConsumer SPI, controller routing) and
        components/engine/engine-bpm-flowable (only needs to resolve client-compiled classes from
        delegate expressions). Extracted from engine-java's runtime package so engine-bpm-flowable
        can depend on this small leaf module instead of the full engine — that in turn lets
        components/api/api-modules-java publish the org.eclipse.dirigible.sdk.* annotations to
        engine-java without forming a cycle through api-bpm.

items.title:
ai.ravenroot:ravenroot-observability-otel 0.5.1-alpha.1 发布, PLAT-01: the OpenTelemetry export bridge, spans, metrics and
        log-correlation identifiers derived from ai.ravenroot.api.application.ExecutionEvent, the
        same event ai.ravenroot.server.audit.StructuredExecutionLogger already consumes. Depends on
        ravenroot-application-api (the event shape) and ravenroot-core (ExecutionMonitor.subscribe,
        the only extension point this module uses) and nothing else in the ai.ravenroot tree. Neither
        of those two modules, nor ravenroot-application-api's other consumers, every third-party
        node package, depends on this one: the OpenTelemetry SDK is reachable from exactly one kind
        of caller, a composition root (RavenrootServerMain, RavenrootCliMain), which is what makes
        "no OpenTelemetry dependency in core" a property the compiler enforces rather than prose.
        Disabled unless RAVENROOT_OTEL_ENABLED is set; see
        TelemetryConfiguration. Every OpenTelemetry artifact here is Apache License 2.0; this module
        has not been through the release SBOM and licence scan and should be before it
        ships in a tagged release.

        It works on Linux/Windows and MacOS for applications created in JVM, CLR/Netcore, Perl, Python, Ruby, NodeJS, C++ or GoLang and gives you unparalleled freedom and flexibility with native performance in building your mixed-technologies products.
        Let it be accessing best AI or cryptography libraries, devices SDKs, legacy client modules, internal custom packages or anything from public repositories available on NPM, Nuget, PyPI, Maven/Gradle, RubyGems or GitHub.
